title: Operator audit signal reconciliation and SLO refinement
creator: Samira Lopez
description: Goal: reconcile differences between RBAC v2 decision telemetry and centralized audit ingestion, define measurable SLOs for auth/audit signal availability and latency, and produce an actionable alert tuning and post-incident closure runbook. Scope includes: 1) mapping event sources (AuthZ API, proxy sidecar, SSO/SAML provider webhooks, on-prem audit forwarders) to ingestion pipelines; 2) instrumenting gaps where policy-eval events are missing or duplicated; 3) defining SLOs for audit ingest success rate (per-region) and auth decision latency; 4) tuning existing Grafana/Alertmanager rules to surface real incidents, not noise; 5) producing a runbook and a retrospective with follow-ups. Out of scope: RBAC policy model changes or SAML provider upgrades themselves (those will be separate tickets).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Inventory of all event producers with example traces/log lines and ownership documented in Confluence; 2) New SLO definitions checked into slo-config repo and visible in the observability dashboard; 3) Alert rules updated with reduced false positives (target reduction > 80% in one week) and documented playbook for escalation; 4) Post-incident retrospective artifact created with clear owners for follow-ups; 5) End-to-end test harness that simulates a policy decision and verifies it appears in the audit index within target latency.
updates: 2026-02-24 — Ticket created. Initial triage meeting held with EngSec, Observability, and Platform teams. Decided to focus first on ingestion and latency SLOs before tackling anomaly detection ML models.

2026-02-27 — Inventory workshop completed. Identified four event producers: api-authz (primary decision service), edge-proxy (envoy sidecar logs), saml-webhooks (IdP event notifications), and onprem-forwarder (customer-side batched uploads). Owner contacts recorded in Confluence page: /confluence/auth-observability/event-inventory.

2026-03-02 — Found two classes of mismatch: (A) duplicated events when edge-proxy and api-authz both emit decision logs for the same request, and (B) missing decision logs for long-tail policy checks (>100ms) caused by sampling in the decision service. Decided trade-off: keep proxy sampling off for now (higher ingest cost) to ensure complete auditability; revisit sampling with prefix caching and dedup later.

2026-03-04 — Implemented temporary dedup key in ingestion pipeline (kafka consumer) to reduce duplicate-indexing while we remove proxy duplication at source. Prototype PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5123 (ingest: de-dupe by request_id + event_type).

2026-03-06 — SLO proposal drafted and pushed to slo-config: 1) Audit ingest success rate >= 99.8% (5m windows, per-region) 2) Auth decision observability: 99.5% of decision events ingested within 5s of decision emission 3) Decision API p95 latency < 120ms (for policy-eval path). PR: github.com/redwood-inference/slo-config/pull/88. Requested review from @Marcus Patel (Observability) and @Isha Rao (Security).

2026-03-08 — Alert tuning session: narrowed noisy alert rule (audit-ingest-error-rate) to trigger only when error rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m and when backed by spike in kafka consumer lag. Added a secondary alert for degraded ingest latency. Patch: grafana/alerts/audit_rules.yaml#L120-180.

2026-03-09 — End-to-end test harness checked in: tests/auth-observability/e2e_simulate_decision.py. The harness creates a synthetic user request that goes through edge-proxy -> api-authz -> ingestion pipeline and asserts the event appears in ES within configured latency. Test runs in CI (buildkite) and is flaky in us-west-2; created follow-up ENG-24679 to stabilize the test infra.

2026-03-10 — Draft runbook published in Confluence: /confluence/auth-observability/runbooks/ingest-slo-runbook. Includes troubleshooting steps, run commands for consumer offsets, and escalation matrix. Requested Design review for runbook diagrams from @Maya Ortega.
postmortem_summary: Not a single large outage but multiple small incidents over the past quarter revealed noisy alerts and partial visibility into auth decisions. Root causes: duplicated event emission and sampling in decision path. Remediation prioritized to ensure audit completeness before reintroducing sampling for cost control. Follow-ups include: stabilize e2e test infra (ENG-24679), add proof-of-delivery acknowledgements from Kafka producers, and add lineage metadata to events for easier reconciliation.
next_steps: Get security review approval for temporary proxy sampling disablement (security@redwood.ai)
Merge PRs for de-duplication and SLO config; coordinate a small migration window to avoid indexing bursts
Run a controlled chaos test to validate alert fidelity (simulate kafka consumer lag) with Observability on-call
Hand off final runbook to Ops and schedule a runbook drill in next cycle
Create follow-ups to add unique provenance fields to events (request_id, span_id, producer_id) to simplify future reconciliation
